## zarf_package_documentation

Extract and parse the documentation a Zarf package carries.

Write it as `colonel_byte.zarf.zarf_package_documentation`. It runs the installed zarf on the node the task is delegated to; nothing is installed on the cluster's nodes.

Added in `colonel_byte.zarf` 0.33.0.

Runs `zarf package inspect documentation` against a local package tarball, an `oci://` reference, or a deployed package name, and returns the extracted files.

Zarf packages every file named in its `zarf.yaml`'s top-level `documentation:` mapping into a documentation layer, which this module extracts without deploying anything.

Each extracted file is returned as text in `documents`, keyed by its documentation key, and parsed into `parsed` when it is YAML or JSON. A file that is neither is returned as text only, rather than failing the task.

The `prerequisites` key is the one this collection has a format for. When the package carries one and it declares `apiVersion: colonel-byte.dev/v1alpha1` and `kind: PackagePrerequisites`, it is also returned as `prerequisites`; see the `prerequisites` role, which checks a cluster against it.

Signature verification is zarf's `if-possible` unless `verify` says otherwise, so an unsigned package extracts cleanly even when `public_key` is given.

Runs on the node the task is delegated to (typically localhost).

### Parameters

| Parameter     | Type            | Required | Flag       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | --------------- | -------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `package`     | `str`           | yes      | None       | Path to a local package tarball, an `oci://` reference, an `https://` URL, or a deployed package name.                                                                                                                                 |
| `keys`        | `list` of `str` | no       | `--keys`   | The documentation keys to extract. Left unset, every key the package carries is extracted. Naming a key the package does not carry is not an error: zarf extracts what it has, and the key is simply absent from `documents`.          |
| `destination` | `path`          | no       | `--output` | Directory to extract into. Zarf creates a `&lt;package-name&gt;-documentation` subdirectory of it, and `directory` reports the subdirectory it created. Left unset, a temporary directory is used and removed before the task returns. |
| `public_key`  | `path`          | no       | `--key`    | Path to the public key a package signature is verified against. Supplying it does not by itself require a signature: zarf verifies when it can and passes an unsigned package otherwise. Set `verify: always` to reject one.           |
| `verify`      | `str`           | no       | `--verify` | When to verify the package signature. Left unset, zarf's own default applies, which is `if-possible`. One of `never`, `if-possible`, `always`.                                                                                         |
| `kubeconfig`  | `path`          | no       | None       | Path to the kubeconfig file, used when extracting from a package already deployed to a cluster.                                                                                                                                        |
| `zarf_binary` | `path`          | no       | None       | Path to the `zarf` CLI binary on the delegated host. When omitted, `zarf` on `PATH` is used.                                                                                                                                           |

### Notes

- Set `run_once: true` and `delegate_to: localhost` on the task.
- The module runs in check mode and reports `changed: false`. It writes files, but only the ones it extracts, and only under `destination` or a temporary directory of its own - nothing on the cluster or in the package changes.
- Left unset, `destination` is a temporary directory that is removed before the task returns, so `files` names paths that no longer exist. Set it when a later task has to read a file rather than its contents.

### Example

```yaml
- name: Read the prerequisites a package declares
  colonel_byte.zarf.zarf_package_documentation:
    package: /srv/staging/zarf-package-operator-external-secrets-amd64-2.12.0.tar.zst
    keys:
      - prerequisites
    public_key: /etc/zarf/colonel-byte-zarf-packages.pub
    verify: always
  delegate_to: localhost
  run_once: true
  register: pkg_docs

- name: Report the Flux version the package requires
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "{{ pkg_docs.prerequisites.metadata.package }} requires flux {{ pkg_docs.prerequisites.requires.fluxcd.version }}"
  when: pkg_docs.prerequisites is defined

- name: Keep the extracted documentation for a later task to read
  colonel_byte.zarf.zarf_package_documentation:
    package: oci://ghcr.io/colonel-byte/packages/app-fluxcd:2.9.5
    destination: /srv/staging/documentation
  delegate_to: localhost
  run_once: true
  register: pkg_docs

- name: Show where it landed
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "{{ pkg_docs.directory }} holds {{ pkg_docs.files | dict2items | map(attribute='value') | list | join(', ') }}"
```
